verification_scope: the force attribute on APP_ENV, which was already verified, PLUS the eight keys the suite depended on but never declared - the Recommended Improvement's remaining half, and the reason this entry was held at mitigated. All eight are now in the tracked <php> block of api/phpunit.xml: COMPANY_SALES_INBOX_EMAIL, COMPANY_CERTIFICATION, COMPANY_LOGO_PATH, COMPANY_EMAIL_BRAND_NAME, ACCOUNTING_FUNCTIONAL_CURRENCY_CODE, ADMIN_NAME, ADMIN_EMAIL, ADMIN_PASSWORD, each with a comment naming its consumer. None is forced: the attribute stays on APP_ENV and that entry only, because forcing an entry lets this file outrank CI's job-scoped env, which is the defect this entry already documents for DB_HOST, DB_DATABASE and DB_PASSWORD. Values are derived from the code's own fallbacks rather than chosen: EmailBrandingService::data() for the COMPANY_* keys, the literal migration 0358 inserts for the sales inbox, the literal migration 0309 inserts for the functional currency, and empty for COMPANY_LOGO_PATH because that is migration 0123's default and api/.env.example's value and no template renders company.logo_path. NOT claimed, and stated plainly in the Status note: the suite asserts none of these eight values, and the three ADMIN_* keys are not exercised by it at all, since AdminUserSeeder is reachable only through DatabaseSeeder and no test seeds DatabaseSeeder. What is verified is the Ideal Process itself - the suite's declared configuration is the configuration it runs in, and it no longer varies with an untracked file.
regression_proof: Machine-dependence measured rather than inferred, on a worktree holding no env file at all (no api/.env, no api/.env.testing), which .github/workflows/api-tests.yml:66 confirms is also the CI-shaped state. A probe test reading env() for all eight keys returned NULL for all eight beforehand. Adding an untracked api/.env.testing carrying hostile values then returned every one of them, COMPANY_CERTIFICATION=HOSTILE-CERT and ACCOUNTING_FUNCTIONAL_CURRENCY_CODE=USD among them: a gitignored file (.gitignore:12) fully controlled the suite's configuration, which is the half of F-042 that was still open. After declaring the eight, the same probe with that same hostile file still in place returned the pinned values, byte-identical to the run with the file deleted. FULL SUITE RUN TWICE, both on dedicated databases and neither on the shared ogami_test: without APP_ENV in the process environment, 1848 tests / 9169 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors, exit 0; with APP_ENV=testing passed as a process variable, 1848 tests / 9169 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors, exit 0. Identical counts, not merely both green. The two runs were also shown to BE the same state rather than assumed equivalent: the probe reported the process APP_ENV and app()->environment() as 'testing' in both, because the force attribute writes the variable into the process environment either way. NET BEHAVIOUR DELTA, derived key by key: exactly one resolved value moves. company.certification goes from '' to a non-empty string, so PDF letterheads now render the certification line they carry in production. The other seven are byte-identical no-ops, because a migration or an in-code fallback already supplied them - migration 0358 for the sales inbox, migration 0309 for the currency, SettingsSeeder's own fallback for the email brand name, migration 0123's empty default for the logo path, and nothing at all for the three ADMIN_* keys. So no latent failure was repaired and none of the eight gained coverage; what changed is which artefact decides the values. One correction made before commit: a first draft of the new ACCOUNTING_FUNCTIONAL_CURRENCY_CODE comment claimed the setting seeded as '' and that four requiredString() readers threw on reach. That was false - migration 0309 inserts the literal PHP, and the key sits in SettingsSeeder's deploymentKeys where a blank env value skips the write rather than blanking the row. Prior mitigation evidence retained: on a working copy holding api/.env.testing, 1900 tests / 9388 assertions / 0 errors / 0 failures; an earlier forced run reporting 65 errors was discarded as contaminated by a concurrent writer on the shared ogami_test, not reported as fallout.
